note: Contract between the bridge firmware and everything that consumes it (panel firmware, Home Assistant, Mi Home, Node-RED). Neither side imports the other's code; both are generated from or validated against this file.
device_id_note: Last 6 hex digits of the heater BLE address, lower case. Stable across reflashes, so entities survive a firmware update.

state.purpose: Full device snapshot, published when a value changes or every keepalive interval.

availability.purpose: Last will is 'offline'. A consumer must treat a missing state plus 'offline' as unknown, not as zero.

set_temperature.purpose: Setpoint. The bridge ignores out-of-range values rather than clamping.

command.purpose: Operational commands. 'refresh' asks for an immediate state publish.

attributes.purpose: Slow-changing metadata: firmware version, heater address, uptime, pairing state. Separate topic so it is not repeated in every state message.

state_fields.label: Active fault code
state_fields.note: Two upper-case hex digits, or 'none'. Never an empty string - a consumer drawing a fault badge needs a definite value.

state_fields.label: Bridge timestamp (epoch)
state_fields.note: Set by the bridge, not by the heater. Consumers detect a stalled bridge by an ageing ts.

device.identifiers_note: device_id already starts with 'btwh_', so prefixing it again would yield btwh_btwh_<last6>. The identifier is the device_id itself.
device.name: Water heater

home_assistant.entity_note: One entity per state field. Sensors use state_class measurement; setpoint is a number entity; flame is a binary_sensor; mode is an enum sensor; fault is a sensor with an icon template.

consumer_rules: A missing field means 'not reported yet'. Do not print it as 0 - an unheated heater and an unreachable bridge must look different.
fault == 'none' is healthy; any other value is a fault code, not text.
availability == 'offline' overrides state: show 'unavailable' and stop drawing the last value as current.
Never hard-code the base topic in firmware: generate it from this file or read it from the bridge's attributes.

producers.python/tools/: a reference publisher, useful when testing a panel without a bridge

consumers.firmware/panel/: planned touch panel; generates its UI binding from state_fields
consumers.integrations/homeassistant/: planned integration; generates entities from the same list
consumers.firmware/bridge/: publishes; must pass the contract test before release

source_of_truth: state_fields keys are checked against python/bosch_api.py::DeviceState by python/tests/test_mqtt_contract.py; renaming a field there without updating this file fails CI.
